title: tri-sdk-credential-retry-and-streaming-ergonomics-unification
author: Ayesha Patel
release_notes: Consolidates credential profiles and retry defaults across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Adds ergonomic streaming consumer helpers, explicit retry profile presets, and small API surface parity fixes. Bumps SDK minors where necessary.
description: Context: Cross-team customer feedback and internal telemetry showed inconsistent retry behavior and awkward streaming APIs across the Python/TS/Go SDKs (retries misaligned with server-side SLOs, credential priming gaps, and inconsistent async iteration ergonomics). Motivation: provide a single behavioral contract for credential lifecycles and retry semantics so polyglot clients behave predictably and so examples/docs can be shared. Summary: this PR unifies the credential profile model (SessionProfile / CredFactory), introduces pinned retry presets (fast-fail, balanced, conservative) with deterministic jitter math, and adds a small ergonomic layer for streaming consumers: async generator adapter (TS), AsyncIterator sugar (Python), and PullStream helper (Go). The change set includes implementation in all three SDKs, updated cross-sdk integration tests, docs and migration notes, and a minor version bump for TS/Go. Checklist: - [x] design review with ENG-4827/ENG-4891 - [x] implement CredFactory in Go, SessionProfile in Python, credential adapter in TS - [x] add retry presets and deterministic jitter util shared in docs - [x] add streaming consumer helpers and examples - [x] update changelogs and migration guide - [x] run cross-sdk integration tests and fix parity gaps Compatibility: default behavior is backwards compatible; existing clients inherit previous behavior unless they opt-in to the new SessionProfile/cred presets. Migration: documented short recipe for Python/TS/Go (see docs/migration/tri-sdk-cred.md). Testing: unit tests for each SDK (auth/retry), cross-sdk integration matrix (tokens scoped, refresh flow, stream resume), and manual validation against a local dev server simulating auth edge cases. Rollout: staged release—cut new JS minor and Go minor; publish Python patch with opt-in flag; monitor runtime metrics for token churn and retry rates. Notes: kept the public surface minimal (small constructors and helper functions), added deprecation warnings where we replaced older helpers to ease transition.

testing_notes: Unit tests added for auth and retry in each SDK. Cross-sdk integration matrix runs a local token server to exercise refresh and stream resume; smoke examples executed manually. Added a benchmark for Go PullStream to ensure no per-chunk allocation regression. CI flake addressed by deterministic jitter and extended test timeout.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: default behavior preserved; opt-in APIs provide the new ergonomics. Biggest risk is a regression in long-lived streams if token-refresh edge cases differ in customer environments; mitigated by integration tests and expanded manual smoke runs. Monitoring targets added to detect token churn and retry storms post-release.
